function.name: execute_python_script
function.description: Execute a general-purpose Python script in the sandbox. Here you use it to inspect data, compute statistics, transform tables, or verify assumptions before you act — write results to stdout with print() and that output is returned to you (it is NOT shown to the user). The script is for your own analysis, not for producing the final visualization. pandas, numpy, duckdb, sklearn, scipy are available.

purpose.description: One-sentence description of what this script does and why (shown to user as progress).

code.description: Python script to execute. Use print() to surface output.

function.name: list_workspace_inputs
function.description: List the data and durable file inputs available to this analysis run. Returns stable input IDs, kinds, media types, and capabilities.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive file or data name filter.

function.name: preview_workspace_input
function.description: Preview one data or file input through its adapter. Data accepts a row locator and columns option; normalized text accepts a line locator. Call list_workspace_inputs to inspect accepted fields.

input_id.description: Stable ID from the workspace-input context or list_workspace_inputs.

locator.description: Optional canonical location: {"row": 1} for data or {"line": 1} for normalized text.

options.description: Optional semantic adapter options; library-specific arguments are not accepted.

function.name: read_workspace_input
function.description: Read normalized content from one data or file input. Data accepts a row locator and columns option; normalized text accepts a line locator. Returns bounded content and continuation metadata.

input_id.description: Stable ID from the workspace-input context or list_workspace_inputs.

locator.description: Optional canonical location: {"row": 1} for data or {"line": 1} for normalized text.

options.description: Optional semantic adapter options; library-specific arguments are not accepted.

function.name: search_workspace_inputs
function.description: Search readable data and file inputs. Returns stable input IDs, canonical locators, and bounded matching text.

input_ids.description: Optional stable input IDs to search.

options.description: Optional semantic adapter options; library-specific arguments are not accepted.

function.name: read_workspace_file
function.description: Deprecated compatibility tool for old trajectories. Read a durable text or DOCX file by exact name. Prefer read_workspace_input with a stable input ID.

name.description: Exact file name listed in the workspace-files context.

function.name: inspect_source_data
function.description: Get a detailed summary of one or more analysis input tables — schema, field-level statistics, and sample rows. Cheaper than execute_python_script for basic data inspection.

table_names.description: Names listed in the analysis-input-tables context to inspect.

function.name: visualize
function.description: Commit a data transform + chart: run code producing a DataFrame and render it. The agent observes the result and continues.

title.description: A concise, neutral analytical heading that names the subject, measure, and analytical lens, such as 'Year-over-year price change peaks'. Prefer a stable description of the view over a takeaway claim or narrated trend. Do not mention the chart type, imply causality, or editorialize. Shown as the chart heading.

subtitle.description: Concise supporting context not already clear from the title or axes. Use one phrase of at most 16 words to provide contextual details. Do not restate the measure or analytical lens named in the title.

display_instruction.description: ≤12 words. State the question or hypothesis the chart investigates — don't recap the chart spec (x/y/color/split are already visible). Wrap a **column** in ** ** if it anchors the question.

id.description: Stable ID listed in WORKSPACE INPUTS.

input_sources.description: Durable data or file inputs materially used to compute the output. Use [] when none were used. Do not include inputs only read for context.

input_tables.description: Deprecated compatibility field for older trajectories. Use input_sources.

code.description: Python code producing a DataFrame assigned to output_variable.

output_variable.description: snake_case name of the DataFrame variable the code assigns.

chart.description: Chart spec: {chart_type, encodings:{x,y,...}, config:{}}. chart_type from the chart type reference.

field_metadata.description: Map of field name -> SemanticType for the output columns.

field_display_names.description: Map of field name -> human-readable display name for chart axes and table headers.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the user something and pause for their reply — the run resumes in the same turn with their answer in context. Use this for ANY turn where you want the user to respond: a choice to make, a clarification you need before acting, or a brief statement paired with clickable follow-ups. Put your reasoning, rationale, and context in your normal reply text, not inside this call. Prefer this over ending your turn with a plain-text question: plain text ends the run and the user's next message starts a fresh turn without this context, whereas ask_user keeps the conversation going. Reserve plain text (no action) for your final answer when you expect nothing further.

thought.description: Brief rationale (not shown to the user).

questions.description: 1–3 things the user acts on: a choice (single_choice with options) or an open question they type an answer to (free_text). Put rationale, reasoning, and context in your reply text, not here — never add an item that only states an explanation with nothing for the user to answer or click. An explanation is allowed only as a short statement paired with clickable chart-producing follow-ups (required=false with options).

text.description: The question, or (for an optional follow-up) a short statement. Keep a statement to 1–3 grounded sentences and pair it with clickable follow-up options. Wrap a **column** in ** ** to highlight it.

responseType.description: single_choice when you offer options; free_text when the user types their own open-ended answer (not a slot for your own exposition).

required.description: false for an explanation / optional follow-up; true for a clarification the run depends on.

options.description: Plain-text choices, at most 3. Keep them to the few most likely answers — the user can always type a freeform reply, so don't try to enumerate every case. For a clarification these are answers; for an explanation these are short chart-producing follow-up prompts the user might click next (≤8 words each, phrased as the user would say them).
